messages.subject: rstan install compiled at -O0?
parts:
It looks like RStan is just using -O0 for building the
various object files. This is totally OK for the parser,
but is there a way to make sure they install at -O3 for
everything else? I looked on the R getting started
guide:

http://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted

and I seem to recall there were instructions for tweaking
the R compiler config, but I don't see them anywhere in the
doc. Can you bring those back? I think this is orthogonal
to the set_cppo() usage.

Jiqiang -- could you create for each platform (Mac, Windows,
Linux) a simple install checklist with checkpoints that
the user can test are installed successfully (checkpoints
like you did for Rcpp). I think
that'll make it a lot easier for relative novices in R like
me to make sure I'm installing things the right way. Otherwise,
I'm worried people will do what I just did and wind up
with a slow install of Stan.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] rstan install compiled at -O0?
parts:
I think you have used set_cppo('debug') and did not set back to set_cppo('fast'). 
The flags setting is tricky.  It is not orthogonal to set_cppo(). If set_cppo() is used, 
the settings, which stays until a different calling of set_cppo(), will overwrite everything
set in the makefile (use O3 for everything) in package rstan.

On Fri, May 17, 2013 at 12:02 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
It looks like RStan is just using -O0 for building the
various object files.  This is totally OK for the parser,
but is there a way to make sure they install at -O3 for
everything else?  I looked on the R getting started
guide:

http://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted

and I seem to recall there were instructions for tweaking
the R compiler config, but I don't see them anywhere in the
doc.   Can you bring those back?  I think this is orthogonal
to the set_cppo() usage.

I took them away as if a user has never used set_cppo(), O3 set 
in the makefile of rstan package will be used.  If set_cppo() is used, 
I am assuming it is always 'fast' while 'debug' is just used temporarily. 
Now I guess it is a wrong assumption.

Jiqiang -- could you create for each platform (Mac, Windows,
Linux) a simple install checklist with checkpoints that
the user can test are installed successfully (checkpoints
like you did for Rcpp).
I tried to do that but did not find a satisfying results.  I will try again.

I think
that'll make it a lot easier for relative novices in R like
me to make sure I'm installing things the right way.  Otherwise,
I'm worried people will do what I just did and wind up
with a slow install of Stan.

Absolutely right. The solution is to delete file
~/.R/Makevars or set_cppo('fast') before removing the older package.  
I should more words to the getting started wiki webpage, thought it would be wordy, 
but it should avoid such problem.


- Bob

No. The Mac binaries are only up to R 3.0.0. Not that
I would've read the NEWS.html file anyway.

I managed to get everything back the way I wanted it as
I reported in the speed run (which by the way had the
relative speed results we were expecting). -O0 vs. -O3
makes a really big difference!

> http://cran.r-project.org/src/base/NEWS.html
>
> Maybe this can help us?

These two jumped out at me:

UTILITIES

R CMD config now make use of personal ï¿½Makevarsï¿½ files under ï¿½~/.Rï¿½ and a site file ï¿½Makevars.siteï¿½, in the same way as
R CMD SHLIB and R CMD INSTALL. This makes the utility more useful in package configure scripts.

On Windows finding the personal files may require the environment variable HOME set.

The old behaviour can be obtained with the new options --no-user-files and --no-site-files.

PACKAGE INSTALLATION

Alternatives to the site and user customization files ï¿½Makevars.siteï¿½ and ï¿½~/.R/Makevarsï¿½ can be specified via the
environment variables R_MAKEVARS_SITE and R_MAKEVARS_USER respectively. These can be used to suppress the use of the
default files by setting an empty value (where possible) or a non-existent path.

- Bob

would set O3 for everything.  So typically there is not problem for users without any 
version of rstan installed before.

This is tricky. Did you see that R 3.0.1 has made some changes here? See the part about R CMD config at

No.  The Mac binaries are only up to R 3.0.0.  Not that
I would've read the NEWS.html file anyway.

I managed to get everything back the way I wanted it as
I reported in the speed run (which by the way had the
relative speed results we were expecting).  -O0 vs. -O3
makes a really big difference!


http://cran.r-project.org/src/base/NEWS.html

Maybe this can help us?

These two jumped out at me:

UTILITIES

R CMD config now make use of personal ‘Makevars’ files under ‘~/.R’ and a site file ‘Makevars.site’, in the same way as R CMD SHLIB and R CMD INSTALL. This makes the utility more useful in package configure scripts.

On Windows finding the personal files may require the environment variable HOME set.

The old behaviour can be obtained with the new options --no-user-files and --no-site-files.

PACKAGE INSTALLATION

Alternatives to the site and user customization files ‘Makevars.site’ and ‘~/.R/Makevars’ can be specified via the environment variables R_MAKEVARS_SITE and R_MAKEVARS_USER respectively. These can be used to suppress the use of the default files by setting an empty value (where possible) or a non-existent path.

- Bob

parts:
R 3.0.1 for Mac is out. 

I have checked out using R_MAKEVARS_USER environment variable.  If R_MAKEVARS_USER is set, $HOME/.R/Makevars will be replace by what $R_MAKEVARS_USER.  So for installing rstan, we can set it to empty so that the makefile (which sets O3 flag) in rstan package will not be overwritten. 

I have changed the RStan getting started a bit: for users who have already installed a version of rstan, executing set_cppo('fast') is suggested before installing.
